_read_me: offboarding-completeness suite (config/benchmarks/offboarding-completeness.json). Each key is a Prisma model with a direct `studentId` FK to Student that src/lib/student-archive.ts's generateStudentArchive() does not read (checked by whether the Student relation field that model hangs off is selected in the archive query). Exempt a model here ONLY when its rows are non-personal bookkeeping or a value fully derivable from data the archive (or the app's own re-derivation) already keeps elsewhere — never because it would be inconvenient to add. Every other not-exported model is a real export-completeness gap and stays reported at watch tier for the owner to prioritize; this file must not grow to cover them without a stated non-personal/derivable reason per entry.
Progression: Single-row aggregate `{ state, version }` used to drive the client's journey-step UI. Holds no free text and is deterministically re-derivable from the underlying ProgressionEvent ledger (also exempted below) plus the static progression rules — there is nothing here a student wrote or said.
ProgressionEvent: XP-award ledger entries (`eventType`, `sourceType`, `sourceId`, `xp`, timestamps). Bookkeeping for the gamification layer, not narrative content — the underlying action each entry points at (a completed task, a verified cert) is the actual record of what the student did, and several of those source tables are already in the archive.
LlmCallLog: AI-call metering only: `callSite`, `model`, token counts, `durationMs`, `promptRevision`. Never stores the prompt or the reply — no conversation content lives here, only what it cost to run. The actual conversation content is in Message, which is a separate, real gap this suite reports (not exempted).
PasswordResetToken: Authentication artifact: a token hash and its expiry, structurally identical in kind to Student.passwordHash, which the archive also does not (and should not) export. Not decodable, not informational to the student, and by the time of an export most rows are already expired or consumed.
SecurityQuestionAnswer: Authentication artifact: a hashed security-question answer. Same reasoning as PasswordResetToken — the hash cannot be turned back into the student's original answer, so including it would hand the student a value they cannot read and that has no evidentiary meaning outside the login flow.
